correctness.rationale: All-n proof: the (k,r) chain partitions the k^2-r feasible edges; the terminal obstruction is equivalent to R_1=1. The first-moment conditional identity telescopes to the exact nonnegative defect sum. The independently proved contraction E[(R_k)_2] <= k^4/n^2 produces 0 <= 2/(n+1)-Q_n <= 16H_n/n^2. Exact rational recurrence, independent subset-state dynamic programming and the full 720 edge orders at n=3 agree. Finite tests are supplementary, not infinity proofs.

value.rationale: The crown graph is the canonical one-factor deletion of K_(n,n), a natural model of one forbidden partner per entity. Sharp failure risk, rather than matching ratio, is a specific and practically interpretable invariant of the greedy process. The 2/n constant differs from the 1/n independent-survivor benchmark and arises from the exact preserved-overlap mechanism. The finite-n harmonic bound and factorial-moment lemma make the result useful beyond isolated numeric computation, though no extension to arbitrary forbidden-edge patterns is claimed.
